options: The invoice distribution references an invalid or incorrect GL account combination
A price variance against a purchase order
A supplier's expired business classification
A closed GL period
questions.explain: Account holds flag invoice distributions pointing at invalid or incorrect account combinations.

questions.q: Which type of hold is specifically tied to quantity or price differences against a purchase order or receipt?
options: Account hold
Matching hold
Supplier site hold
Funds hold
questions.explain: Matching holds are raised when invoice quantities or prices vary from the PO/receipt beyond configured tolerance.

questions.q: How does an automatically-releasable, application-placed hold typically get cleared?
options: It never clears and the invoice must be cancelled
Only Oracle support can clear it
By fixing the underlying issue and running validation again, which clears the hold as part of re-validation
It clears itself after 30 days regardless of the underlying issue
questions.explain: Many application-placed holds clear automatically once the underlying condition is corrected and validation runs again.

questions.q: What is true about certain system holds, like a line or distribution variance hold?
options: They can be released with a simple button click, no correction needed
They automatically release after any invoice edit
They only apply to credit memos
They cannot be released manually; they are only removed by correcting the invoice and revalidating
questions.explain: Certain system holds require correcting the underlying issue and revalidating; they cannot simply be manually released.

questions.q: Can a single invoice carry more than one hold at a time?
options: No, only one hold is ever allowed per invoice
Yes, unrelated holds (e.g. an account hold and a matching hold) can be present simultaneously, each needing its own resolution
Only if the invoice type is Mixed
Only if the supplier is international
questions.explain: Because validation checks multiple independent conditions, an invoice can accumulate several unrelated holds at once.
